instructions: Continue only from the exact clean transportable RUN-191-001 failed candidate ac5a0afb3734a8e709515a86589e18a64e201be1. Preserve all compatible TASK-191 r1 implementation already present; do not restart TASK-191 from main or discard the failed candidate.

The canonical failure is Runtime verification only: python -m pytest -q tests/test_gemini_reviewer_transport.py returned 27 passed, 2 setup errors because pytest expanded the 262145-byte parametrized bytes value into the test node id / PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST environment variable on Windows, exceeding the 32767-character environment-variable limit before the affected test bodies ran. Treat this as a test-harness identifier defect, not evidence of a production GeminiReviewerTransport defect.

Modify only tests/test_gemini_reviewer_transport.py. Keep src/aios_renew/gemini_reviewer_transport.py and src/aios_renew/schemas/gemini_reviewer_semantic_response.json byte-for-byte unchanged unless Runtime later exposes a distinct production defect; if any production change appears necessary, stop unresolved rather than widening this repair.

Preserve the oversized native-output coverage and every TASK-191 acceptance property while keeping pytest node ids bounded. Use explicit short deterministic ids for the parametrized failure cases and/or construct oversized payloads inside the test body from short descriptors. No test id may contain the full large payload.

Do not weaken the existing malformed UTF-8/JSON, duplicate-key, non-finite-number, invalid-status, missing-structured-output, missing/invalid usage witness, cache-alias disagreement, nonzero-exit, timeout, workspace-cleanup, exact-one-call, read-only capability, P3 composition, fingerprint-invariance, authority-isolation, no-raw-payload, and offline-only assertions.

Do not add a suite-wide pytest hook, modify tests/conftest.py, pyproject.toml, Runtime, workflow, Reviewer protocol, executor profile, roadmap, or any file outside modification_scope in this repair. The repeated Windows node-id issue is a separate maintenance concern because TASK-191 explicitly limits mutation to its three original paths.

Runtime exclusively owns canonical verification. Return the complete TASK-191 structural ResultPackage with claims covering AC1 through AC8 and no claim that Executor-run tests are canonical evidence, that BP-8 is complete, or that Gemini is a default/preferred Reviewer.

acceptance.condition: A dedicated Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash Reviewer proof transport exists with no implicit registration/default activation: model is proof-bound to gemini-3.8-flash, effort is explicit with no default, and existing Reviewer provider selection plus executor-profile policy remain unchanged.

One exact JsonReviewerProvider request up to the canonical request bound is delivered byte-for-byte through a fresh isolated temporary workspace rather than command-line embedding; the native command remains bounded independently of request size, exposes no repository path, and the workspace is removed on success and every tested failure.

The native Reviewer invocation is demonstrably read-only and single-provider: exactly one process call uses only the selected Gemini model, explicit effort, bounded structured-output/time mechanics and the isolated request workspace, with no Executor mutation flags, repository/Git capability, second provider, retry, fallback or reroute.

Valid provider-native structured output is normalized into the exact existing JsonReviewerProvider wrapper and then validated by the unchanged BP-6 P3 protocol into an AIOS_REVIEW_DECISION; the new output schema/parser performs transport shaping only and does not duplicate semantic REVIEW validation.

Native nonzero exit, timeout, malformed/duplicate/over-bound output, invalid status, missing structured output, invalid provider-native witness and invalid P3 semantic response all fail closed after at most one native process call using the existing pre-REVIEW failure boundary, without canonical REVIEW, RUN failure, remediation, retry or fallback.

Successful calls expose only bounded immutable transient operational observation sufficient for later BP8-P2 attribution—request digest, Antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash identity, explicit effort, one-call count and validated native usage/call witness—while retaining no raw request/response, credentials, environment, reasoning/session content and creating no canonical EVIDENCE.

Static and behavioral tests prove role/authority isolation: no import/reuse of Executor adapters or execution-profile routing, no Runtime/ingress/Publisher dependency, no repository mutation/discovery authority, no change to existing Reviewer contracts/defaults, and operational attribution does not change semantic request/decision fingerprints.

The entire TASK-191 verification is deterministic and offline with injected runners only, covers the dedicated BP8-P1 production and schema surfaces, and explicitly proves that no real provider invocation or BP-8 completion claim is made; the resulting path is ready only for a separately authorized BP8-P2 real call.

assumptions: Canonical planning at 9af9713e9c79bcc0b3a71f73ae4d8a7ec2289f66 records BP-7 complete, BP-8 as the unique NEXT milestone, and explicit Human/Brain selection of the Antigravity native transport with model gemini-3.8-flash as the first real Reviewer proof only; this is not a default-provider decision.
src/aios_renew/reviewer_provider.py and src/aios_renew/reviewer_provider_protocol.py remain the authoritative BP-6 one-call invocation and semantic request/decision validation surfaces.

The existing Reviewer request is bounded to 2097152 UTF-8 bytes and provider semantic response to 196608 bytes by the reviewed protocol, while JsonReviewerProvider independently bounds the native wrapper to 262144 bytes.

Existing Antigravity native execution code is Executor-specific reference material only. Its repository access, execution-profile policy, mutation flags, ResultPackage semantics and Executor instruction contract must not be imported or reused as Reviewer authority.

BP8-P2, not this TASK, owns the first real provider invocation and Runtime-owned evidence that proves an actual remote Gemini call. TASK-191 verification is deterministic and offline with an injected process runner only.

hard: Mutation is limited exactly to the three paths in scope.modify. If a correct implementation requires changing an existing Reviewer protocol/provider, Executor adapter/profile, workflow, Runtime, ingress, publication, roadmap, package configuration, or frozen specification, stop with an unresolved item rather than widening TASK-191.

The production path is proof-specific, not a new default: it is bound to the selected Antigravity native transport and model gemini-3.8-flash. No module import, registration side effect, global configuration, executor profile, or Reviewer protocol may cause this path to be selected implicitly.

Reasoning effort is operational input for the later proof and must be supplied explicitly by the caller with no TASK-191 default. Invalid or absent effort must fail before native process invocation; the transport must not read the Executor execution-profile policy to obtain one.

The transport must accept the exact strict-JSON request bytes supplied by the existing JsonReviewerProvider callable boundary. It may enforce transport byte bounds and compute operational digests, but it must not reinterpret, augment, truncate, summarize, or independently validate Reviewer semantics.

Full Reviewer request bytes must never be embedded in the native command line or prompt argument. Each invocation must create one fresh isolated temporary workspace outside repository authority, write the exact request bytes there, expose only that bounded workspace to the native process, and remove the workspace on both success and failure. Repository paths, Git/GitHub handles and unrelated filesystem paths must not be exposed to the model.

The provider instruction must be transport-minimal: identify the transient REVIEWER role, direct the model to consume only the supplied exact AIOS_REVIEW_REQUEST and its embedded procedure/return-contract material, forbid repository/Git/GitHub discovery and mutation, and require only the semantic response shape. It must not add semantic review criteria, acceptance answers, verdict preferences, hidden prior context, or provider-specific reasoning content beyond what the request already contains.

The schema added by this TASK is a native output-shaping schema only. It may constrain the outer provider semantic response needed by P3, but must not duplicate the REVIEW grammar, acceptance/finding semantics, P2B return-contract validator, review.validate_review, or any semantic authority already owned by the BP-6 protocol.

Native invocation must be read-only and single-shot. It may select only the fixed model gemini-3.8-flash plus the explicit caller-supplied effort and bounded structured-output/time-limit mechanics. It must not pass accept-edits/dangerous mutation permissions, grant repository access, run shell/Git operations on behalf of Reviewer, invoke another model, or retry, reroute or fall back after any failure.

The provider-bound parser must independently and strictly validate the native process envelope needed for transport: bounded UTF-8 output, successful native status, one mapping structured_output, and a bounded provider-native usage/call witness. Duplicate/malformed JSON, nonzero process exit, timeout, missing structured output, missing/invalid witness, or over-bound output must fail closed as transport/response failure and never fabricate a REVIEW or lifecycle state.

Successful native material returned to JsonReviewerProvider must contain only the semantic_response plus the existing closed operational attribution fields. Provider/model attribution must identify the selected Antigravity / gemini-3.8-flash proof path. Session/invocation identifiers may be null when the native transport does not provide verified values; synthetic identifiers must not be invented merely to look attributable.

Any provider-native usage/call observation retained after the call must be immutable, bounded, transient operational metadata only. It may bind the exact request-byte digest, configured provider/model/effort, invocation count and bounded native usage/call witness, but must retain no raw request, raw response, credential, environment snapshot or reasoning trace and must never label itself canonical EVIDENCE. BP8-P2 Runtime-owned evidence remains the only authority for the future real-call proof.

The transport must neither inspect nor serialize credentials. Authentication may be inherited by the native CLI from the Human-controlled environment in BP8-P2, but command arguments, temporary files, normalized observations, error messages and test fixtures must contain no secret value or environment dump.

Focused tests must use only injected deterministic process runners and fresh temporary fixtures; they must never launch agy or another external provider. Tests must prove maximum-bound request delivery does not grow the command with request content, isolated workspace cleanup, exact one-process-call stop semantics, read-only capability flags, strict envelope/output bounds, and successful composition through the existing JsonReviewerProvider plus P3 validation.

Focused tests must also prove authority isolation: the new transport has no dependency on codex_adapter, antigravity_adapter, execution_profile, Runtime, authoring ingress or publication modules; no existing Reviewer/provider/default file is changed; and provider/model operational attribution cannot alter the request or validated decision fingerprint.

TASK-191 completion means only that the dedicated offline BP8-P1 path is reviewed and ready for a separately authorized BP8-P2 controlled real invocation. It must not claim real-provider evidence, Gemini quality, provider preference, BP-8 completion, or downstream readiness.

task.goal: Establish BP8-P1 as one deterministic, offline, provider-bound real-Reviewer proof transport for the Human-selected Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash path, capable of carrying one exact existing AIOS_REVIEW_REQUEST v1 through a repository-blind read-only native invocation boundary and returning material consumable by the already-reviewed Reviewer provider shell, without making Gemini a default Reviewer, performing a real external invocation in this TASK, or changing Reviewer/lifecycle authority.
non_goals: Make Gemini 3.8 Flash, Antigravity, or any provider/model the default Reviewer or preferred Reviewer.
Add a provider registry, model scorer, selector, router, retry, fallback, failover, voting, consensus, or automatic provider switch.

Modify reviewer_provider.py, reviewer_provider_protocol.py, REVIEW schema, review.validate_review, Decision Packet, Unified State, Runtime, ingress, Publisher, terminal attention, or frozen Kernel semantics.
Import or reuse codex_adapter.py, antigravity_adapter.py, execution_profile.py, Executor policy, ResultPackage mechanics, or Executor repository/mutation permissions as Reviewer authority.
Perform a real Gemini/Antigravity invocation, require live credentials, access the network, or claim the BP-8 exit gate in TASK-191 verification.
Persist provider prompts, raw native responses, reasoning traces, chat/session state, credentials, environment contents, or a provider memory store.
Create a generic provider-native transport abstraction intended for arbitrary future providers.
Submit a canonical REVIEW, author remediation/repair, publish, mutate roadmap state, or create any lifecycle state from the provider transport.
Modify workflows, operator commands, repository defaults, executor profiles, existing tests, or downstream repositories.
task.problem: BP-6 proves a provider-neutral one-call Reviewer protocol with independent non-network adapters, and BP-7 proves fresh-context/provider continuation, but AIOS does not yet have a reviewed provider-bound native transport surface that can be used for the first controlled real non-default Reviewer proof in BP8-P2. Reusing the Antigravity Executor adapter would merge role mechanics and grant unnecessary repository/mutation authority, while embedding the complete Reviewer request on a Windows command line is unsafe because the canonical request may be much larger than practical command-line limits. BP8-P1 therefore needs only a narrow, isolated, read-only Gemini Reviewer transport that composes with the existing Reviewer protocol and leaves the later real call and canonical evidence to BP8-P2.
